reading_log.notes: Read complete contributions/related work and sequential-DAG embedding formulation, exact authors/Microsoft affiliation and ICLR2019 header; differentiable objective training differs from RL and from label-based NeuroSAT.

Read all sequential forward/reverse GRU aggregation and recurrence equations, circuit encoding, variable soft-assignment decoder and smooth fixed evaluator/loss. Temperature-limit intuition does not replace checking the original Boolean circuit.

Read exact test-time replacement of smooth gates by min/max and no-false-positive claim, SAT-only training/test selection, matched-size300k paired generation, full training hyperparameters, generalization bars/time claims and graph-coloring data/circuit preprocessing.

Read all graph-coloring results, explicit mismatch with NeuroSAT original protocol and open explanation, discussion/limits and entire bibliography through Deep Sets. Scientific method not claimed competitive with industrial solvers.

Read all integrated AppendicesA-D, classification variant, complete threshold/no-false-positive argument and proofs, CNF cube expansion/order heuristic and graph-coloring encoding. Note strict threshold tie subtlety in printed negation lemma.

claims.statement: Direct assignment discovery and circuit-aware propagation target limitations of CNF SAT classification proxies.
Forward/reverse sequential GRU DAG layers reuse recurrent weights and predict variable assignments.
A nontrainable smooth evaluator supplies differentiable loss; test-time min/max replaces smooth gates.
Only SAT training examples are used experimentally, despite label-free objective form.
AppendixB connects exact min/max evaluation to positive witnesses; strict-threshold NOT identity has an exact0.5boundary caveat and negative candidates do not proveUNSAT.
The unchanged random-kSAT-trained model transfers via circuit encodings to graph-coloring decision tasks, supporting reduction-based generalist reuse.
Graph-coloring transfer is48%/27%inSATselected tiny-graph datasets; discrepancy with original NeuroSAT result remains unresolved.
Training oneGPU/day and roughly180kparameters; circuit expansion and variable-order heuristics add work beyond neural iterations.
